passage: Coach's note, Tuesday. Tanvir stayed behind after nets and asked if he could talk. "Sir, I want to speak to Omkar," Tanvir said, "but he's the captain and everyone likes him. If I go first, won't I look desperate?" I asked what Tanvir wanted to say. "That the catch on Saturday was really good." I said that sounded honest, and simple honest lines often work better than clever ones. The worry, I think, is about being judged, not about Omkar. Tanvir practised it once, then took a breath and walked over. Omkar said, "Thanks, that ball was slippery!" and they talked kit bags until the bus.

qa.q: What did Tanvir want to say to Omkar?
qa.a: That the catch on Saturday was really good.

qa.q: What was Tanvir afraid of when asking to speak to the captain?
qa.a: Looking desperate by talking first to someone everyone likes, a fear of being judged.

qa.q: What did the coach do that helped Tanvir decide to speak?
qa.a: The coach asked what Tanvir wanted to say and pointed out that the honest, simple line was a good one.

qa.q: How did Omkar respond to Tanvir?
qa.a: Omkar answered warmly, saying thanks and that the ball was slippery, and they chatted until the bus, so the first line was welcome.

grounding: A teenager fears talking first to a popular peer looks desperate, and a simple honest opener works.

passage:
Friday, 9 pm. I wrote three opening lines for Vikas on the back of my rough copy. One was a pun. One was about the physics test. One was so clever I crossed it out because it didn't even sound like me. All I could think was, what if he thinks I'm trying too hard? I kept picturing Vikas walking away. Then at the corridor stall today I just said, "Hey, I really liked your poster." Nothing else. Vikas smiled and said, "Thanks, I worked on it all week." That was it. I walked home surprised how ordinary it felt. Maybe simple was always enough.
Lalit

qa.q: What did Lalit say to Vikas at the corridor stall?
What was Lalit worried about while writing the opening lines?
qa.a: That trying too hard would look bad, and picturing Vikas walking away, a fear of being judged.

qa.q: What did Lalit decide at the stall, and why did it work?
qa.a: Lalit dropped the clever lines and said one honest thing about the poster, which was easy to answer.

qa.q: What might Vikas be feeling when hearing about the poster?
qa.a: Pleased that the work was noticed. Vikas smiled and said it had taken all week.

grounding: A teenager worries talking first to someone will look desperate, and finds a simple honest opener works.
